title: Local topological dimension formula for smooth morphisms
statement:
Let $g:P\to Q$ be a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] between locally Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth]. For any $p\in P$, set $q=g(p)$ and let $P_q=P\times_Q\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(q)$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], with its point corresponding to $p$. With local topological dimensions as in [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point],
$$ \dim_p P=\dim_q Q+\dim_p P_q.$$
Here local topological dimension is the infimum of the dimensions of open neighbourhoods, not the dimension of the local ring. In particular, when $g$ is smooth of constant relative dimension $d\geq0$, the last summand is $d$.

proof.text: Fix $p\in P$ and put $q=g(p)$. The statement of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension] gives a non-negative integer $d=\dim_p(P_q)$. By [sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant], choose an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq P$ of $p$ such that $\dim_a(P_{g(a)})=d$ for every $a\in U$. This is a neighbourhood on the source; no constancy across different connected components of $P$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0AFF, lemma-smoothness-dimension, first sentence of proof; Tag 02G1, lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free

proof.text: Let $h=g|_U:U\to Q$. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat], $g$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. An open subscheme has the restricted structure sheaf [def-weil-open-immersion], so its stalk at $a\in U$ is the stalk of $P$ at $a$; the stalk map of $h$ is consequently the stalk map of $g$, hence flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Also $U$ is locally Noetherian by the open-subscheme clause of [pqf-def-locnoeth]. For any affine open $V\subseteq Q$, cover $h^{-1}(V)$ by affine opens $W$ of $U$, which are also affine opens of $P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], each corresponding algebra is a quotient of a polynomial algebra over $\mathcal O_Q(V)$ in finitely many variables. The images of those variables generate it. This is exactly the affine-cover condition of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], so $h$ is locally of finite type. No finite subcover is used.

source.place: Tag 0AFF, proof: flat and locally of finite type; Tags 01VF, 01VE and 01TQ (1) implies (2)

proof.text: For any $a\in U$ put $b=g(a)$. By the topological description in [def-pc-scheme-fibre], the underlying spaces of $U_b$ and $P_b$ are respectively $U\cap g^{-1}(b)$ and $g^{-1}(b)$, with their subspace topologies. Thus $U_b$ is an open subspace of $P_b$ containing the point corresponding to $a$. The open-subspace equality [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] gives $\dim_a(U_b)=\dim_a(P_b)=d$, the last equality being Step 1. Consequently every point of every nonempty fibre of $h$ has local topological dimension $d$. Empty fibres require no assertion.

source.place: Tag 0AFF, proof: after shrinking, relative dimension d; Topology Tag 0055, definition-Krull and following remark

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-flat-constant-relative-dimension] to $h:U\to Q$ and $d$. Both schemes are locally Noetherian, $h$ is flat and locally of finite type by Step 2, and its fibre dimensions at all points are $d$ by Step 3. Since $p\in U$ and $h(p)=q$, it yields $\dim_p U=\dim_q Q+d$. No claim that $h$ is surjective is needed by the cited statement.

source.place: Tag 0AFF, final sentence of proof, applying Tag 0AFE (lemma-rel-dimension-dimension)

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] for the open neighbourhood $U$ of $p$ in $P$: $\dim_p P=\dim_p U$. Substitution in Step 4, followed by $d=\dim_p(P_q)$ from Step 1, gives $\dim_p P=\dim_q Q+\dim_p(P_q)$ as required. These are equalities in the extended nonnegative dimensions, so the substitution also applies when $\dim_q Q=+\infty$.

source.place: Tag 0AFF, conclusion; Topology Tag 0055, definition-Krull and following remark

proof.text: If $g$ is smooth of constant relative dimension $e\geq0$, [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] says precisely that $\dim_p(P_q)=e$ at every $p$, so the last summand is $e$. The dimension used throughout is the neighbourhood minimum of [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]; no equality with the dimension of the local ring has been used. If $P$ is empty, both assertions quantified over $p\in P$ are vacuous.
